disease_relevance: AS, revised New York criteria; not all axSpA

context.functional_PBMC_donors: 7 ERAP1-001 homozygotes versus 4 ERAP1-002 homozygotes, all AS/HLA-B*27:04
context.allotype: study-local ERAP1-001 and ERAP1-002 labels; not automatically Hap1/Hap2
context.assays: Sanger full-length cDNA; TaqMan SNVs; PBMC PMA 10 ng/mL 48h then LPS 1 microgram/mL 16h; CHO/U937 expression; immunoprecipitated enzyme fluorigenic assay
context.treatment_context: not sufficiently described for confounding adjustment

limitations: Sex imbalance: 717/863 male cases versus 706/1438 controls; sex-adjusted association
Small functional donor subset and technical replicates
HLA-B27-positive case/control haplotype comparison not significant
Methods describe fluorigenic conditions but do not unambiguously identify the substrate sequence; do not manufacture it
Discussion-like inference that 002 is risk in B27-negative is supported by stratified controls, not just case-case comparison
No pharmacological direction or engagement test
rationale: Adds ancestry-specific association and functional allotype evidence, including primary patient PBMC context; not merely a SNP association.
findings: Study-local ERAP1-001 was enriched among AS cases versus controls (adjusted OR 1.53, 95% CI 1.35–1.73).
In HLA-B27-negative participants, ERAP1-002 was associated with AS versus HLA-B27-negative controls (adjusted OR 1.69, 95% CI 1.15–2.49).
The small HLA-B*27:04 AS PBMC comparison linked ERAP1-001 to higher ERAP1, FHC/UPR markers and IL-23 than ERAP1-002; CHO expression also differed.
impact_rationale: Strengthens target biology and genotype-context rationale, not inhibition efficacy.

disease_relevance: HLA-B27 transgenic experimental SpA; not human axial disease remission

context.model: 33-3 HLA-B*27:05/human beta2-microglobulin transgenic rats, mixed Lewis/Sprague-Dawley
context.phenotype: peripheral arthritis, epididymoorchitis, stool and colon histology
context.blinding: clinical caretakers and histology readers blinded

limitations: Germline prevention is not reversal by a drug
Multiple transgene copies and rodents without ERAP2
No human clinical efficacy
Compartment-specific FHC effects
No single disease-wide beneficial direction
rationale: Direct perturbational disease-model evidence with meaningful divergent outcomes.
findings: Arthritis frequency was 12/37 with ERAP1 versus 4/34 without ERAP1 (p=0.03); severity and onset among affected animals were comparable.
ERAP1 loss did not improve stool scores and increased colon histology scores.
ERAP1 loss reduced intracellular HLA-B27 misfolding/UPR but increased surface free heavy chains and dimers.
ERAP1 loss reduced excess Il23a induction but did not restore defective dendritic-cell stimulation or the depleted CD103-positive population.
impact_rationale: Improves perturbational support while weakening a uniformly beneficial inhibition narrative.

disease_relevance: AS revised New York criteria; mechanistic adaptive immune context, not therapy

context.population: Italian recruitment, ancestry not explicitly established
context.hla: 102 B*27:05 subjects (93 AS/9 healthy); 11 B*27:09 controls; 13 B*07 carriers
context.genotype: four-marker ERAP1/ERAP2 haplotype, not full ERAP1 protein allotype
context.peptides: pEBNA3A RPPIFIRRL, pDYNEIN RPPIFGDFL, RPXXXXXXL cocktail
context.dose: pEBNA3A 20 microgram/mL; pDYNEIN 40 microgram/mL initial culture
context.controls: APC medium subtraction, EBV serology, alternative HLA subtypes, T2 stabilization

limitations: Long ex-vivo expansion and arbitrary responder threshold
Healthy-donor cross-reactivity limits disease specificity
Dynein residue numbering differs between Results and Methods; retain peptide sequence without asserting a resolved coordinate
Not direct immunopeptidome mass spectrometry
No engagement or chemical-genetic test
rationale: Links ERAP1/2 haplotype context to HLA-B27-restricted antiviral/self cross-reactive cellular responses.
findings: The four-marker CCAG ERAP1/ERAP2 haplotype was enriched in pEBNA3A nonresponders among B*27:05 carriers (73 responders/29 nonresponders; haplotype p=0.0179).
Expanded B*27:05-restricted pEBNA3A responses could cross-react with the dynein self peptide; responses also occurred in healthy donors.
impact_rationale: Adds adaptive-immune context without establishing pathogenic causality or intervention direction.

disease_relevance: Contextual ERAP1 biology; not AS patient intervention

context.population: 2504 phased 1000 Genomes samples, five major ancestry groups
context.allotype: ten recombinant full-length common allotypes, noncleavable C-terminal 6-His tag
context.compounds: DG013A active-site inhibitor; GSK849 regulatory-site modulator
context.replication: peptide trimming triplicates; allotype-10 enzyme concentration increased where specified

limitations: Activity sums assume independent alleles and do not model expression differences
Substrate-specific rank cannot be generalized to every peptide
No AS cellular engagement or clinical evidence
rationale: Provides functional allotype and substrate dependence relevant to selecting experimental constructs.
findings: Ten common recombinant ERAP1 allotypes differed in substrate-dependent trimming and intermediate accumulation; YTAFTIPSI catalytic efficiency differed up to 60-fold.
GSK849 activated Leu-AMC hydrolysis but inhibited YTAFTIPSI trimming, with allotype-dependent potency; DG013A inhibited all ten allotypes in the Leu-AMC assay.
impact_rationale: Strengthens the requirement to specify allotype and peptide substrate rather than assign universal activity labels.

disease_relevance: Contextual allotype mechanism, not disease rescue

context.allotype: allotypes 1/10 and allotype-10 V349M, Q725R, double mutant; insect expression with C-terminal TEV/10-His construct
context.compounds: DG013A and GSK849; source contains inconsistent GSK labels in some captions
context.conditions: peptide 10 micromolar, enzyme concentration adjusted by construct; 1h 37C triplicates; GSK849 10 micromolar peptide experiment
context.controls: wild-type allotypes, verified mutations, solvent controls

limitations: Not an AS cohort
Substrate concentration and kinetic model affect interpretation
Compound label discrepancies retained; no new exact chemical identity asserted
rationale: Directly tests the simplification that protective allotype 10 is uniformly inactive.
findings: Allotype 10 was much less active than allotype 1 for YTAFTIPSI but more active for LRVYEKMALY; V349M/Q725R effects also depended on substrate.
Allotypes 1 and 10 showed different substrate-concentration kinetics and DG013A inhibition patterns; GSK849 modulation also depended on polymorphism and substrate.
impact_rationale: Contradicts a universal low-activity interpretation of allotype 10, not the established association itself.

disease_relevance: Tool pharmacology, HeLa antigen presentation and rat PK; not AS efficacy

context.construct: paper reports Hap2 for biochemical assay; PDB construct mapping requires separate reconciliation
context.cell: HeLa flow-cytometry SIINFEKL presentation, not ERAP1 occupancy
context.compounds: paper-local cyclohexyl acids 1, 2, 7, 13; structures depicted in source and bound in linked PDB
context.replication: main tables n>=3 unless stated; ERAP2/IRAP counter-screen of 7 n=1
context.chemical_identity: paper/PDB ligand bridge only, tested-form/stereochemistry not promoted to verified registry substance
context.supporting_methods: main methods sufficient for listed qualitative assertions; SI not inspected in this addendum

limitations: Detailed SI and form/structure standardization required before quantitative learning import
Different substrates/constructs and biochemical versus cellular endpoints
No intact-cell engagement or genetic-dependency readout
GSK author employment conflicts disclosed
rationale: Adds experimentally observed regulatory-site ligands and improved tool pharmacology; do not pool the potency values into baseline datasets.
findings: Main text assay description and Tables 1–2
Optimization improved peptide-trimming inhibition and HeLa SIINFEKL-presentation activity; hit 1 lacked measurable cellular activity despite biochemical activity.
Compound 7 had reported ERAP2 and IRAP pIC50 <4.0 with n=1, using Arg-AMC and Leu-AMC respectively; these are not directly comparable to ERAP1 peptide-substrate potency.
Figures 2/4/5; Data availability; RCSB entry records
Ligand-bound ERAP1 structures were reported for compounds 1, 2, 7 and 13 (9GJN/9GK6/9GJS/9GKE), deposited in 2024 and released in January 2025.
impact_rationale: Improves chemistry/structure options but does not resolve baseline compounds' cellular engagement.

disease_relevance: Contextual ERAP1 conformational mechanism; not AS efficacy

context.assays: SAXS/WAXS, crystal structures, Leu-AMC/Leu-pNA and peptide assays
context.compound: study compounds 2/3 linked to historical Maben chemistry; not cyclohexyl compound 3
context.replication: two independent activity experiments with triplicates; SAXS independent-experiment limits reported
context.controls: apo protein, open/closed structural models and distinct ligand classes

limitations: Preferred compound docking pose is not a measured binding pose
Conformation under saturating purified-protein conditions is not cellular engagement
2023 correction adds facility acknowledgement, not changed scientific results
rationale: Adds orthogonal conformational evidence relevant to allotype-sensitive pharmacology.
findings: The allosteric modulator 3 induced ERAP1 closure in solution; Lys528/Arg528 altered potency for closure-inducing DG013 and modulator 3 but not inhibitor 2.
impact_rationale: Supports construct-specific mechanism without promoting structural behavior to occupancy in AS cells.

disease_relevance: A375 melanoma and THP-1 leukemia; contextual, not AS patient evidence

context.compound: source compound 3: 4-methoxy-3-(N-(2-(piperidin-1-yl)-5-(trifluoromethyl)phenyl)sulfamoyl)benzoic acid; not Maben compound 3
context.dose: 10 micromolar, 0.1% DMSO, 6 days for omics; 48h downstream assays
context.replication: 2 biological immunopeptidome replicates/3 technical; 4 A375 and 3 THP-1 proteome biological replicates
context.control: KO, WT, vehicle; no dose-matched inhibitor-in-KO epistasis/rescue experiment

limitations: A375 KO 1G5 omics clone had partial genomic duplication; downstream experiments switched to 1B12
Healthy-donor cytotoxicity assay not patient-derived disease efficacy
KO/inhibitor concordance is not demonstrated compound dependency
Technical images/replicates are not additional donors
rationale: Accessible orthogonal perturbations reveal non-identical peptidome and broader cellular effects.
findings: Chemical inhibition and ERAP1 KO produced distinct A375 immunopeptidomes despite both perturbing peptide presentation.
Proteomic and ROS changes accompanied ERAP1 disruption; shared effects do not isolate direct peptide processing from indirect cellular pathways.
impact_rationale: Keeps indirect/context explanations viable and cautions against equating inhibition with loss of protein.

disease_relevance: Melanoma/psoriasis-context HLA-I biology, not direct AS/HLA-B27 evidence

context.model: A375 KO clone 1B12 reconstituted with single ERAP1 allotype 2 or 10
context.controls: selected clones with comparable ERAP1 expression
context.replication: 3 separate biological cultures, 2 DIA technical runs plus 1 DDA per sample; one selected clone per allotype
context.analysis: W6/32 purification, LC-MS/MS, 1% FDR, differential log2>=1/q<=0.05
context.sequence: full construct sequences source Figure S1, not imported as verified protein registry identities

limitations: Clone effects not excluded by multiple independent clones per allotype
Predicted HLA affinities are not measured binding
No normalization to a healthy immunopeptidome and no therapeutic benefit endpoint
rationale: Cellular allotype re-expression complements purified-enzyme findings without disease extrapolation.
findings: Expression-matched allotype-2 and allotype-10 A375 clones differed mainly in peptide abundance, also in length and predicted HLA assignment; allotype 10 retained cellular trimming activity.
impact_rationale: Supports allotype/HLA-specific measurements, not a universal functional knockout interpretation.

context.methods: allele-harmonized inverse-variance fixed/random effects, cohort sensitivity, fine-mapping/cTWAS
context.hla: B*27 dosage unavailable, no conditional B*27 analysis

limitations: Reuses public cohorts; not an independent replication of studies using the same biobanks
Substantial heterogeneity and cohort sensitivity
ERAP1 not among seven listed cTWAS-colocalization convergent genes
No experimental ERAP1 knockdown; Jurkat follow-up concerns other genes
AS phenotype ascertainment relies on public GWAS datasets, not harmonized clinical recruitment

impact_rationale: Reinforces biology but neither validates inhibition nor demonstrates ERAP1-specific experimental causality.
